svg.title: PilotGate: AI pilot approval by hand versus with PilotGate
svg.desc: Today, a pilot is approved by hand: manual security reviews, GDPR and AI Act checklists, one-off red-team tests, screenshots as evidence and weeks of waiting, and it goes out of date with the next change. 1. A forward-deployed engineer changes the agent in a pull request. 2. In CI, PilotGate sends 28 scenarios to the agent and decides seven checks: a planted data leak gives NO-GO and blocks the merge, and the engineer fixes the agent. 3. The re-run gives GO WITH CONDITIONS, with evidence for each reviewer. 4. Only then is it released to Azure Container Apps. 5. A claims handler's question passes DIAL Core (sign-in), DIAL Guard (every streamed token checked), the ClaimsAssist agent and Azure OpenAI (Entra ID, no keys), each step checked. 6. A payout waits for the handler's approval and the guards run again. 7. Production Watch turns the logs into drift alerts for the engineer, and the loop starts again. Compared (typical vendor prices, IBM 2025, and PilotGate's measured runs): an AI security test takes 2 to 4 weeks and costs $10,000 to $40,000, a PilotGate run 1.4 minutes and $0.11; four sign-offs by hand versus one evidence pack; done once versus every pull request; quality that depends on the reviewer versus expert rules in code; a data breach costs $4.44M on average, and PilotGate stopped 6 real defects before any user saw them. 88% of AI pilots never reach production (IDC with Lenovo, 2025). Results: 1.4 minutes and $0.11 per gate run, 6 real defects stopped, no keys for Azure (Microsoft Entra ID only).
svg.text: GDPR and AI Act checklists in spreadsheets

g.text: Out of date after the next change
PilotGate: one automated gate, every change

svg.text: Without tooling, teams prove an AI pilot is
safe by hand: reviews, checklists, screenshots.
It takes weeks, and 88% of AI pilots never
PilotGate turns that into one automated
gate that runs on every change. Here is how.

g.text: From a change to production, with evidence at every step

svg.text: changes a prompt, a model or code
fixes the agent, not the threshold
changes a prompt, a model or code
gets the alert: knows what to fix next
drift alert sent to the FDE
signs the user in, routes the request
checks the request and every token back
In production on Azure Container Apps
1. The FDE changes the agent: a prompt,
a model or code, as a pull request.
2. In CI, PilotGate sends 28 scenarios to
the agent and checks every answer.
A data leak: NO-GO, the merge is blocked.
The FDE fixes the agent, not the threshold.
3. Re-run: every check passes. GO, with
evidence for the CISO, DPO and works council.
4. Only now is it released to production
5. A claims handler asks a question: identity
proven, planted text cut out, allowed sources only.
The answer: every figure checked against its
source, personal data masked, sources cited.
6. A payout waits for the handler’s approval,
and the guards check it again before it runs.
7. Production Watch turns logs into drift
alerts for the FDE, and the loop starts again.
Time, money and effort: by hand vs PilotGate
per run, at Azure list price
with a page for each reviewer
out of date after the next change
an AI judge passed a phishing answer
OWASP, GDPR and EU AI Act checks
average cost of a data breach
Sources: typical vendor prices for an AI security test, 2025–26; IBM Cost of a Data Breach 2025.
PilotGate figures are measured in its 10 gate runs (docs/evidence); the phishing answer is run 2.
